newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Rwandan president arrives for Kinshasa summit.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan president arrives for Kinshasa summit.

text.p: Rwandan President Pascal Bizimungu arrived in Kinshasa on Tuesday for a summit of key allies who helped Laurent Kabila seize power, officials said.

Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni arrived on Monday. Both leaders have made three previous official visits to Kinshasa since Kabila toppled veteran dicator Mobutu Sese Sese in May and renamed Zaire the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Uganda and Rwanda backed the seven-month armed campaign against Mobutu, spearheaded by ethnic-Tustsis who dominate the Rwandan army.
Separately, Tanzania's retired founding president Julius Nyerere also arrived in Kinshasa for talks with Kabila, but officials said these were separate from the summit.

Officials in Tanzania said Nyerere's visit was to promote reconciliation in the new Congo, where the civilian opposition that battled Mobutu's dictatorship for years is grumbling over being left out of Kabila's government.
Nyerere was expected to visit the provincial towns of Lubumbashi and Kisangani, the officials said.
Kabila's aides said the summit talks, previously scheduled to end on Tuesday, would now stretch for an extra day.
